📚 Scoring Guide & How to Analyse This Report Click any row header to expand detail below
▶  Click to expand — Signal Score, InvScore, card elements, and decision checklist

Every ticker generates two independent scores: Signal Score (technical pattern confluence) and InvScore (composite investment quality across 4 data layers). Both are 0–100. 50 is perfectly neutral. Neither score is financial advice — always apply your own risk rules.

1. Signal Score (0–100) — Technical Pattern Confluence

Weighted average of 9 independent pattern analyses. 50 = neutral. ≥55 leans bullish. ≤45 leans bearish. A score of 75+ with High confidence = strongest entry signal in the system.

PatternWeightName & What it measures
P118%EMA Stack Alignment
EMA 8/21/50/200 ordered & price pulled back to EMA50 (±pullback_pct%). Checks volume confirmation and absence of nearby resistance.
P218%RSI Divergence
Bullish/bearish divergence between price swings and RSI. Also checks hidden divergence, stochastic agreement, and multi-timeframe RSI.
P311%MACD + RSI Cross
MACD histogram cross combined with RSI crossing the 50-line. Lagging — confirms momentum already turning.
P411%MACD Histogram Divergence
Divergence between price peaks and MACD histogram — fires earlier than P2.
P57%OBV Divergence
On-Balance Volume diverges from price. Detects smart-money accumulation into weakness or distribution into strength.
P610%BB Squeeze + RVOL
Bollinger Band contraction (energy coiling) + Relative Volume confirmation. Tight BB + high RVOL = high-probability breakout setup.
P79%Momentum Z-score
How extreme current momentum is vs. the 20-day distribution. Values beyond ±2σ indicate overextension in either direction.
P89%Ichimoku Cloud
Price position vs. Kumo (cloud), TK cross, Chikou span. Confirms structural bullish or bearish bias on a longer timeframe.
Sector RS7%Sector Relative Strength vs SPY
RS > 1.0 = sector outperforming SPY → tailwind. RS < 1.0 = sector lagging → headwind. Reduces score for lagging sectors.

Post-score adjustments applied automatically

AdjustmentEffect
Regime MultiplierBull 1.0×  |  Neutral 0.88×  |  High-Vol 0.75×  |  Bear 0.65× bulls / 0.85× bears — lower regimes compress scores toward 50 because setups are less reliable.
Conflict PenaltyWhen P1 and P2 strongly disagree (e.g. P1=+3, P2=−3), the score is pulled toward 50. High disagreement = uncertain setup.
EMA200 VetoIf the 200-day EMA slope is steeply negative and score > 60, it is pulled back to 50–60. Prevents promoting stocks in macro downtrends.
Earnings CompressionScore compressed toward 50 when earnings are within 3 days. Binary events invalidate technical setups.
52W Low FloorScore capped at 30 for tickers near their 52-week low. Capitulation is not a bullish signal.
B/S Signal BoostActive buy/sell signals from pattern detection add ±4 pts (RVOL confirmed) or ±3 pts to the final score.

Signal Score — Interpretation & Action

ScoreWhat to do
75–100Strong bullish confluence. Multiple patterns agree. High-conviction setup. Favour long entries with clear stop below EMA50.
60–74Moderate bullish. Patterns leaning long. Wait for a trigger candle or volume confirmation before entering.
45–59Neutral. Mixed signals — no clear edge. Stay flat or hold current position. Do not force a trade.
30–44Moderate bearish lean. Patterns weakening. Reduce longs or watch for a breakdown below support.
0–29Strong bearish confluence. Decisive short setup. Avoid new longs. If holding, consider tightening stops significantly.

2. InvScore (0–100) — Composite Investment Quality

Blends 4 data layers into a single quality score. Answers: “Across technicals, chart quality, news, and fundamentals — how strong is this opportunity right now?” Use InvScore to rank opportunities when multiple tickers show BUY signals.

LayerWeightWhat it includes
Tech50% (56%)Signal Score from P1–P8. Already captures EMA structure, momentum, volume, divergences.
Graph22% (32%)BB position, BB width (squeeze), volume trend, volume Z-score, ATR trend, RSI zone. Rewards: coiling BB, accumulation, contracting ATR, RSI 40–65. Penalises: overbought/oversold BB, distribution, expanding ATR.
News10% (12%)Recency-weighted keyword sentiment (Finnhub/NewsAPI). Count-scaled: 1 article=±4pts, 3=±12pts, 5+=±20pts. Weight deliberately capped — free-tier news is 1–3 articles, bag-of-words only. Use headlines as qualitative colour, not a signal.
Fund13% (absent)Fama-French 5 factors + valuation regime context: ROE/ROA (RMW profitability), D/E + Current Ratio (CMA investment conservatism), P/B (HML value factor), P/E regime (at P/E >40, forward returns compress per Navigating Lost Decades), gross/operating/net margins, EPS growth, P/FCF, EV/EBITDA, beta, dividend. Score 0–100 (neutral=50). Only active when yfinance returns balance-sheet data. Percentages in parentheses are weights when fundamentals are unavailable.

InvScore modifiers (applied after layer blend)

ModifierRangeLogic
Ichimoku Bonus+5 / −5Price above Kumo adds +5 (macro bullish structure). Below Kumo −;5. Visible as Ichi +5 chip on the InvScore mini-bar.
RSI Divergence Adj.+6 / −6Hidden bullish divergence adds +6 (covert accumulation). Hidden bearish divergence subtracts 6 (covert distribution). Visible as RSI Div chip.
IV Crush Penalty−10Options implied-volatility crush risk near earnings. Subtracts 10 pts to flag that the stock may be whipsawed. Visible as IV −10 chip.

InvScore — Interpretation & Action

InvScoreWhat to do
80–100High conviction. Strong technicals, quality chart structure, supportive fundamentals/news. Best opportunities for new entries.
65–79Good setup. Most layers positive. Manageable risk. Favour entries with a defined stop.
45–64Average. Mixed picture across layers. No strong edge. Hold, don't add.
30–44Weak. At least one major layer is negative. Reduce exposure or tighten stops.
0–29Poor quality. Multiple layers flagging risk. Avoid new positions. Exit or hedge existing ones.

3. Card Element Reference

Every element visible on a ticker card, what its values mean, and how to act on it.

Card elementValuesHow to read it
Direction badgeBUY SELL HOLDPrimary trade direction decided by the EMA-stack & momentum model. Always check confidence + regime before acting on BUY/SELL.
ConfidenceHigh Medium LowHow many patterns agree AND how strong the market regime is. Low confidence = do not trade regardless of direction.
Signal Score0–100 badgePattern confluence (P1–P8 + Sector RS). Green ≥65, yellow 45–64, red ≤44. Open the Pattern Breakdown panel (▶) to see which patterns fired and why.
InvScore mini-barTech Graph News FundSegmented bar showing each layer's contribution. The number at the far right is the composite InvScore. Chips after the bar show active modifiers (Ichi ±5, RSI Div ±6, IV −10).
Earnings banner⚠ Earnings in N daysOrange = binary event risk. Scores are compressed toward 50. IV crush penalty may apply. Avoid new entries; tighten stops on existing positions.
EMA stackEMA8 / EMA21 / EMA50 / EMA200All green & ordered = fully bullish structure. Any inversion = structural conflict. EMA200 is the macro trend line — price below EMA200 = bearish macro context regardless of short-term signals.
Williams %R−20 to −100Above −20 = overbought (potential reversal down). Below −80 = oversold (potential reversal up). Most useful when it diverges from price direction.
ADX0–100< 20 = no trend (ranging market — trend signals unreliable). 20–40 = moderate trend. > 40 = strong trend. Not directional — measures trend strength only.
DI+ / DI−Directional linesDI+ > DI− = bullish pressure dominant. DI− > DI+ = bearish pressure dominant. Crossovers are early trend-change warnings. Most reliable when ADX > 20.
IchimokuAbove / Inside / Below cloudAbove cloud = macro bullish (institutional confirmation). Below cloud = macro bearish. TK Bullish = Tenkan-sen above Kijun-sen (short-term momentum confirmed).
RVOL-ToDRelative Volume1.0 = average volume. > 1.5 = elevated institutional interest — conviction behind the move. < 0.5 = very low participation — question the breakout. ToD version adjusts for time of day during market hours.
RSI Divergence flagBullish Div / Bearish DivBullish = price made lower low, RSI made higher low (hidden strength). Bearish = price made higher high, RSI made lower high (hidden weakness). Adds/subtracts 6 pts to InvScore when active.
IV Crush flagIV CrushOptions IV crush risk near earnings. InvScore −10. Do not sell options premium into an unknown earnings direction.
Pattern Breakdown (►)P1–P8 barsCollapsible panel. Each bar is centre-anchored: right = bullish confidence, left = bearish. Width = magnitude (±1/±2/±3). Data quality dots show which of the 9 components had actual data — grey dots mean that pattern scored neutral by default.
Conflict flag⚠ ConflictShown in Pattern Breakdown when P1 and P2 strongly oppose each other. The conflict penalty was applied. Do not take a high-conviction position when core patterns disagree.
52W Low flag▼ 52W LowPrice within 5% of 52-week low. Score capped at 30. Capitulation ≠ buy signal. Wait for a confirmed reversal with volume.

4. Decision Checklist — Before Every Trade

Run through these 10 steps in order before opening any position suggested by this report. The goal is to prevent acting on noise.

1
Market regime — Check the regime banner at the top. In Bear or High-Vol regimes, skip bullish setups unless InvScore ≥ 70 AND confidence is High. All scores are already regime-adjusted, but add your own filter on top.
2
Earnings banner present? — If yes → stop. Do not open new positions into a binary earnings event. If you hold, tighten your stop to the nearest support level.
3
Direction + Confidence — Only act on BUY/SELL with High or Medium confidence. Low confidence = signal noise. HOLD = no edge detected.
4
InvScore ≥ 65 — InvScore < 65 = at least one major data layer is weak. Best entries happen when InvScore ≥ 65 and Signal Score ≥ 60 and they agree on direction.
5
Conflict or 52W Low flag? — If the Pattern Breakdown panel shows a conflict flag, the core patterns disagree — halve your normal position size. If the 52W Low flag is shown, do not buy — wait for a reversal candle with volume.
6
EMA200 macro filter — Price below EMA200 = macro bearish context. Only take BUY signals if InvScore ≥ 70 AND there is a clear catalyst. Otherwise, confine to short or neutral positions.
7
RVOL-ToD > 1.0? — Volume below average on a breakout = lack of conviction. Wait for RVOL ≥ 1.0 before entering. RVOL ≥ 1.5 = institutional participation, highest-quality setups.
8
ADX > 20? — If ADX < 20, the market is ranging. Trend-following signals (EMA stack, MACD cross) are unreliable in ranging markets. Favour mean-reversion setups (Williams %R extremes) instead.
9
News — sanity check only — Read the headlines to understand why the stock is moving. Do not trade on news sentiment alone. 1–3 keyword-matched articles ≠ a reliable signal. The news layer carries only 10% of InvScore weight for this reason.
10
Check your own risk rules last — Apply your personal position-sizing rule (e.g. max 2% risk per trade), set a stop-loss at the nearest structural level (usually just below EMA50), and log the trade with the Signal Score + InvScore at entry for review.
